paths.description: Entry URL redirect, age gate, homepage/listing and global chrome

findings.summary: Theme does not respond to the user’s color-scheme preference
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture; the probe reports colorScheme "normal" and no prefers-color-scheme/color-scheme CSS. The existing dark palette remains usable, but browser UI and surfaces are not preference-driven.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and express palette tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), retaining the current dark design as one supported scheme.

findings.summary: State and route changes have no View Transition treatment
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage on a multi-view site, so navigation and menu state changes swap abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and major state changes with same-document or cross-document View Transitions, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listings provide little state-aware orientation
findings.evidence: The homepage is a long category listing, while CSS inspection found no scroll-state queries, scroll progress, directional transitions, or anchor positioning for custom navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight sticky section/progress cue and use platform positioning/fallbacks for menus where appropriate.

findings.summary: The mandatory age gate is an inaccessible custom overlay
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows #disclaimer_background is a DIV with no dialog role, aria-modal, dialog element, or popover; Lighthouse also finds its close button unnamed.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the gate as a modal <dialog> (or fully conforming dialog pattern), give it an accessible name, trap/restore focus, and label every dismiss/choice control.

findings.summary: Dense chrome competes with the content
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show multiple icon rows, side navigation, badges, category controls, and a large global frame around the primary listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Simplify repeated global controls, group secondary destinations behind clearly labelled disclosure, and preserve content-first spacing.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance misses the LCP target
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 6.5 s, FCP 4.5 s, TTI 11.4 s, and performance 0.65. The unthrottled trace was faster (LCP 1.40 s), confirming network/CPU conditions materially affect delivery.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP candidate, reduce render-blocking work, defer non-critical scripts, and retest under Lighthouse mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and poorly cached resources delay content
findings.evidence: HAR evidence identifies a 129 KB parser-blocking stylesheet, a synchronous 93 KB head script, additional classic scripts without defer, and many thumbnails with no useful cache header.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical classic scripts, preserve async where safe, and apply long-lived immutable caching to versioned thumbnails/assets.

findings.summary: The entry page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 387 KiB unused JavaScript (including 80% of xnxx.js) and 123 KiB unused CSS (98% of front.css); HAR shows the main script alone transfers 394 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Split page-specific bundles, remove duplicate jQuery delivery, and load age verification and page modules only when their surface needs them.

findings.summary: Core controls and media links lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports unnamed age-gate and navigation controls plus many unnamed thumbnail links; the image primitive finds 98 of 100 inspected images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon controls explicit accessible names, expose thumbnail titles as link names, label search, and use meaningful alt text or alt="" only when adjacent text fully duplicates it.

findings.summary: Page structure is weak for assistive navigation
findings.evidence: The homepage probe finds no h1/h2/h3 and only a header landmark, while the custom gate is not represented as a dialog. Focus styling is visible, but structure and modal semantics are missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique h1, logical section headings and landmarks, then use native dialog semantics with managed focus.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 in the live viewport meta, preventing users from zooming despite otherwise successful 360 px reflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1; keep width=device-width, initial-scale=1.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic dimensions and responsive sources
findings.evidence: The image primitive finds all 100 inspected images missing width/height and srcset; 11 are oversized, and Lighthouse also finds low-resolution thumbnails stretched on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, provide srcset/sizes, and select variants matching rendered density.

findings.summary: Redirected public pages omit canonical URLs
findings.evidence: The requested host redirects to xnxx.com; probes on both homepage and detail page find no rel=canonical, even though robots.txt permits crawling and sitemap.xml exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referential canonical links on final public URLs and ensure the alias redirect and sitemap consistently name the canonical host.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security headers are incomplete and CSP is weak
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no HSTS, no X-Content-Type-Options, no Permissions-Policy, and a very broad CSP containing unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. X-Frame-Options is present and no client secrets were found.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS and nosniff, define a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and migrate inline/eval-dependent code to nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval.

findings.summary: Most rendered content is unavailable to non-JavaScript clients
findings.evidence: Discoverability evidence measures only 29% raw-to-rendered content coverage. The raw response includes metadata but much of the navigable category/listing content appears only after JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core listings and links, then progressively enhance interactions; ensure the age notice and primary route remain usable without JavaScript.

findings.summary: The image pipeline is not responsive or resource-efficient
findings.evidence: The image primitive finds 100/100 legacy-format images, 100/100 without srcset, 89 below-fold images without lazy loading, and 11 oversized images; HAR transfers 465 KB of images on the gated entry load.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, use srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold thumbnails, and avoid fetching blurred underlying media until age confirmation.
